<description>
When checking whether a gateway replied with NAT-PMP unsupported version (RFC 6887 appendix A and RFC 6886 section 3.5), `PCPRequestPortMap` mistakenly used `PCP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS` (3) and compared only a single byte against `NATPMP_RESULT_UNSUPP_VERSION`.

NAT-PMP result codes are 16-bit big-endian values starting at offset 2 (`NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS`). A 16-bit result code with low byte 1 and a non-zero high byte (such as `0x0101`) would previously be incorrectly treated as `UNSUPP_VERSION`.

This PR fixes the check to use `ReadBE16(response.data() + NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS)` matching the rest of `pcp.cpp` (lines 348 and 390), and uses `NATPMP_HDR_VERSION_OFS` for the version field offset. A unit test is added to `pcp_tests.cpp`.
</description>

<commits>
aa57403920 net: parse NAT-PMP result code as 16-bit BE in PCP fallback

When checking whether a gateway replied with NAT-PMP unsupported version (RFC 6887 appendix A and RFC 6886 section 3.5), PCPRequestPortMap mistakenly used PCP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS (3) and compared only a single byte against NATPMP_RESULT_UNSUPP_VERSION.

NAT-PMP result codes are 16-bit big-endian values starting at offset 2 (NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS). A 16-bit result code with low byte 1 and a non-zero high byte (such as 0x0101) would previously be incorrectly treated as UNSUPP_VERSION.

Use ReadBE16 with NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS instead, matching the rest of pcp.cpp, and use NATPMP_HDR_VERSION_OFS for the version check. Add a unit test covering this case.
</commits>

<patch>
diff --git a/src/common/pcp.cpp b/src/common/pcp.cpp
index dec9212555..9aed7d8bd2 100644
--- a/src/common/pcp.cpp
+++ b/src/common/pcp.cpp
@@ -483,7 +483,8 @@ std::variant<MappingResult, MappingError> PCPRequestPortMap(const PCPMappingNonc
     auto recv_res = PCPSendRecv(*sock, "pcp", request, num_tries, timeout_per_try,
         [&](const std::span<const uint8_t> response) -> bool {
             // Unsupported version according to RFC6887 appendix A and RFC6886 section 3.5, can fall back to NAT-PMP.
-            if (response.size() == NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_SIZE && response[PCP_HDR_VERSION_OFS] == NATPMP_VERSION && response[PCP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS] == NATPMP_RESULT_UNSUPP_VERSION) {
+            if (response.size() == NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_SIZE && response[NATPMP_HDR_VERSION_OFS] == NATPMP_VERSION &&
+                ReadBE16(response.data() + NATPMP_RESPONSE_HDR_RESULT_OFS) == NATPMP_RESULT_UNSUPP_VERSION) {
                 is_natpmp = true;
                 return true; // Let it through to caller.
             }
diff --git a/src/test/pcp_tests.cpp b/src/test/pcp_tests.cpp
index e70b4b1475..63fdfeeef7 100644
--- a/src/test/pcp_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/pcp_tests.cpp
@@ -576,6 +576,43 @@ BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(pcp_ipv4_fail_unsupported_version)
     BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(*err, MappingError::UNSUPP_VERSION);
 }
 
+// NAT-PMP result codes are 16-bit. A result code with low byte 1 but non-zero
+// high byte (e.g. 0x0101) must not be mistaken for UNSUPP_VERSION.
+BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(pcp_natpmp_result_code_16bit)
+{
+    const std::vector<TestOp> script{
+        {
+            0ms, TestOp::SEND,
+            {
+                0x02, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, // version, opcode
+                0x00, 0x00, 0x03, 0xe8, // lifetime
+                0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xff, 0xff, 0xc0, 0xa8, 0x00, 0x06, // internal IP
+                0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44, 0x55, 0x66, 0x77, 0x88, 0x99, 0xaa, 0xbb, 0xcc, // nonce
+                0x06, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // protocol (TCP), reserved
+                0x04, 0xd2, 0x04, 0xd2, // internal port, suggested external port
+                0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xff, 0xff, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, // suggested external IP
+            }, 0
+        },
+        {
+            500ms, TestOp::RECV,
+            {
+                0x00, 0x81, 0x01, 0x01, // 16-bit result 0x0101 (high byte non-zero)
+                0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
+            }, 0
+        },
+    };
+    CreateSock = [this, &script](int domain, int type, int protocol) {
+        if (domain == AF_INET && type == SOCK_DGRAM && protocol == IPPROTO_UDP) return std::make_unique<PCPTestSock>(default_local_ipv4, default_gateway_ipv4, script);
+        return std::unique_ptr<PCPTestSock>();
+    };
+
+    auto res = PCPRequestPortMap(TEST_NONCE, default_gateway_ipv4, bind_any_ipv4, 1234, 1000, g_interrupt, 1, 1000ms);
+
+    MappingError* err = std::get_if<MappingError>(&res);
+    BOOST_REQUIRE(err);
+    BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(*err, MappingError::NETWORK_ERROR);
+}
+
 // NAT-PMP IPv4 protocol error scenarii.
 BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(natpmp_protocol_error)
 {

</patch>
